title: Rosalind and the Salt
premise: Yara Galloway steals memories for the Ledger Guild, trading other people's pasts to keep her own safely blank. When a prophecy written a century ago names tonight's date as the night the Salt—crystallized memory of a dead god—wakes, Yara realizes she is its unwitting carrier: the guild erased her childhood and hid the god's memory inside her. Hunted by the guild's enforcers and courted by heirs of both ancient armies, she must decide whether to surrender the memory, destroy it, or claim it. In the end, Yara refuses all three: she scatters the Salt into the sea of collective forgetting, erasing herself from every ledger and mind—including her own—so that power dies unclaimed rather than inherited.
about_author: I. M. Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging donated letters no one ever came back to read. They write fantasy about what people choose to remember, and live in a coastal town that floods on purpose once a year.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Yara lifts a dying merchant's happiest decade from his head in exchange for coin, feeling nothing where joy should sit. Back at the guildhall, she files the vial among thousands. POV: Yara. Beat: competent loneliness—the reader learns how memory-theft works and how empty Yara has made herself.

chapters.title: Ledgers of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane assigns Yara to audit the Prophecy Vault, a punishment disguised as trust. Among brittle pages she finds a date: tonight. Beside it, a sketch of a woman with her own crooked collarbone scar. POV: Yara. Beat: dread blooming inside routine.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Yara tests the prophecy against the moon charts; the thirteenth turn completes in twenty-six days. She considers running but her forged identity papers have been quietly recalled—someone anticipated her. POV: Yara. Beat: the trap closing before she knew there was a trap.

chapters.title: What the Vial Remembers
chapters.summary: Yara breaks guild law and tastes one drop of her own confiscated childhood vial: salt water, a burning city, a woman singing a name—hers. POV: Yara, with flashback fragments. Beat: hunger for a self she never had.

chapters.title: The Heir of Ash
chapters.summary: A stranger named Dain corners Yara in a memory-den, claiming descent from the army that killed the god. He offers protection in exchange for the Salt he believes she carries. POV: Dain. Beat: charm with a blade under it.

chapters.title: Corvane's Kindness
chapters.summary: The guildmaster reveals he raised Yara after 'finding' her, and gently asks for the Salt back—for the guild's survival, he claims. His kindness feels rehearsed. POV: Yara. Beat: realizing every gift in her life was a leash.

chapters.title: Saltwater Gospel
chapters.summary: Following the song from her vial-memory, Yara finds a drowned chapel where a blind priestess recognizes the melody. The priestess explains the Salt: a dead god's memory, able to remake whoever holds it. POV: Yara. Beat: awe curdling into terror at what sleeps inside her.

chapters.title: A Theft Turned Inside Out
chapters.summary: Guild enforcers raid the chapel; Yara escapes only by stealing the priestess's memories of her, leaving the old woman smiling at a stranger. POV: Yara. Beat: first taste of what her power costs the people she touches.

chapters.title: Dain's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dain saves Yara from the enforcers, then shows her his family vault: weapons keyed to the Salt, waiting a century. He swears he wants to destroy it, not use it. POV: Dain. Beat: alliance built on mutual usefulness and mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Her Name
chapters.summary: Yara infiltrates the guild archive and finds her own entry: not found, but purchased—a baby bought from the war's last survivors. Corvane signed it. POV: Yara. Beat: grief replacing gratitude; inheritance revealed as theft.

chapters.title: Two Armies, One Moon
chapters.summary: The second heir surfaces: Sefra, descended from the god's worshippers, who wants the Salt enthroned again. She demonstrates her power by restoring a beggar's stolen memories—and offers Yara her childhood whole. POV: Sefra. Beat: temptation wearing mercy's face.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Days Ago
chapters.summary: Yara lets Sefra return one hour of her past: the burning city, her mother pressing the Salt into her swaddle. She wakes weeping and furious. POV: Yara. Beat: memory as wound; knowing yourself hurts exactly as much as promised.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Dain discovers Yara met Sefra and calls it betrayal; their alliance shatters in a knife-edge argument. Alone, Yara catches her reflection flickering with someone older. The Salt is waking. POV: alternating Yara/Dain. Beat: isolation deepening on all sides.

chapters.title: The God's Draft
chapters.summary: In dreams, the dead god's memory speaks through Yara—not cruelly, but tiredly, showing her the war from above: two sides, one lie. It asks only to be remembered. POV: dream-Yara. Beat: sympathy for the monster; the seduction of significance.

chapters.title: Corvane Falls
chapters.summary: Sefra's followers storm the guildhall; Corvane, exposed as the buyer of war orphans, is torn down by the people he 'saved.' He begs Yara to remember him kindly. She does—and hates it. POV: Yara. Beat: the corrupter corrupted; pity as the last corruption.

chapters.title: What Power Wants
chapters.summary: With the guild broken, both heirs converge on Yara. The Salt inside her grows louder, offering each of them exactly what they most desire. Yara sees clearly, for the first time, that the memory itself is the war. POV: Yara. Beat: clarity before climax.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Turn
chapters.summary: One night remains. Yara gathers her allies' promises and finds every promise ends with someone holding the Salt. She begins writing her own ledger: a plan no one agreed to. POV: Yara. Beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Chapel of the Thirteenth Moon
chapters.summary: At the drowned chapel under the full thirteenth turn, Dain and Sefra face off while the Salt rises out of Yara like tide. The god's memory offers itself to whichever hand reaches first. POV: Yara. Beat: climax—all inheritances converging on one body.

chapters.title: Unclaimed
chapters.summary: Instead of choosing an heir, Yara opens herself completely and lets the Salt pass through her into the sea of collective forgetting—unclaimed, unmourned, gone. Both heirs reach nothing. POV: Yara. Beat: the refusal that ends a war before it restarts.

chapters.title: Blank Pages
chapters.summary: The price: the Salt takes her memories as it leaves. Yara wakes on the chapel steps knowing her name and nothing else, holding a ledger written in her own hand addressed 'To me.' POV: Yara. Beat: hollow victory; grief without its object.

chapters.title: To Me
chapters.summary: Reading her own instructions, Yara chooses which single memory to restore from a vial she apparently saved: not her childhood, but the priestess's song. She hums it without knowing why, and smiles. POV: Yara. Beat: quiet reclamation—identity rebuilt from choice, not inheritance.

chapters.title: Rosalind and the Salt
chapters.summary: Months later, a thief called Rosalind works the coast roads, keeping a small ledger of memories she gives away free. In the final entry, dated tonight, someone has written a new prophecy: a girl who refused a crown. POV: Rosalind/Yara. Beat: resolution—power dispersed, story begun again on her terms.
